source_book: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum, Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah, Tarikh al-Khulafa, Siyar A'lam an-Nubala
author: Compiled
title: Islamic calendar and history
description: A comprehensive chronology of Islamic history — Prophets, Companions, battles, caliphate and later eras
note: Important events of Islamic history are arranged in detail according to the Hijri months and dates.

items.title: Hijri New Year
items.description: During the caliphate of Umar (R.A.), the Hijri year was calculated based on the migration of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).

items.title: Martyrdom of Umar (RA).
items.description: The 2nd Caliph of Islam Hazrat Umar Ibnul Khattab (RA) was martyred by the stabbing of Abu Lulu Firoz.

items.title: The Caliphate of Uthman (RA) begins
items.description: After the martyrdom of Umar (RA) Uthman (RA) was elected as the third caliph through the Shura Committee.

items.title: The ark of Noah (a.s.) is on Mount Judi
items.description: According to commentators, on this day the ark of Noah (A.S.) settled on Judi Hill after the Great Flood.

items.title: Commemorating the Martyrdom of Zayd Ibn Haresa (RA).
items.description: Zayd (RA), the beloved companion and beloved son of the Prophet (PBUH), was martyred as the first commander in the Battle of Mutah.

items.title: Rescue of Yusuf (a.s.) from the well
items.description: According to commentators, on this day Yusuf (A.S.) was rescued by a caravan from a well abandoned by his brother.

items.title: Liberation of Ibrahim (A.S.) from the fire
items.description: Some narrations say that on this day Allah made the fire of Nimrud cool and peaceful for Ibrahim (A.S.).

items.title: Hussain's (RA) journey to Karbala
items.description: Hussain's (RA) caravan reached the desert of Karbala. Yazid's soldiers stopped the water supply.

items.title: Call Musa (A.S.) to Mount Tur
items.description: Musa (a.s.) was summoned to converse with Allah on Mount Tur and received the Torah.

items.title: Ghazwaye Khaibar
items.description: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) conquered Khaibar, the fort of the Jews, with 1600 companions. Ali (RA) conquered the fort of Kamus.

items.title: The sinking of the pharaoh
items.description: Tasua — The day before Ashura. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to fast on this day as well.

items.title: Ashura - The deliverance of Musa (A.S.).
items.description: Allah saved Musa (a.s.) and Bani Israel from Pharaoh. Pharaoh drowned in the Red Sea.

items.title: The tragedy of Karbala
items.description: Hussain (may Allah be pleased with him), the son-in-law of the Prophet (may peace be upon him) was martyred in Karbala. 72 family members and companions were martyred with him.

items.title: Battle of Kadeshia
items.description: Muslim forces led by Saad bin Abi Waqqas (RA) defeated the Persian commander Rustam.

items.title: Gazwaye Jatur Rika
items.description: Campaign against the Gatafan tribe of Najd. The rule of Salatul Khawf (Prayer of Fear) was revealed in this battle.

items.title: Yunus (A.) Deliverance from the belly of the fish
items.description: According to the narration, Yunus (A.S.) was released from the belly of the fish by the grace of Allah around Ashura.

items.title: Battle of Talut and Jalut
items.description: The army of Bani Israel led by Talut defeated the army of Jalut. Dawood (A.S.) killed Jalut.

items.title: Martyrdom of Ammar Ibn Yasir (RA).
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) predicted that Ammar would be killed by the rebel group. He was martyred at Siffin at the age of 93.

items.title: Succession of Sulayman (a.s.).
items.description: After Dawood (A.S.) his son Sulaiman (A.S.) received the kingship and prophethood.

items.title: Ayyub (a.) relief from disease
items.description: After a long illness, Allah Ta'ala granted health to Ayyub (A.S.).

items.title: Death of Imam Abu Hanifa (RA).
items.description: Imam Azam Abu Hanifa Numan bin Thabit (RA), the founder of Hanafi Fiqh, passed away in Baghdad.

items.title: Death of Zainul Abedin (Rah.).
items.title_ar: وَفَاةُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ زَيْنِ الْعَابِدِينَ
items.description: Ali Ibnul Hussain Zainul Abedin (R.A.) son of Fera Hussain (R.A.) survived Karbala and passed away in Madinah.

items.title: Conquest of Egypt
items.description: The Muslim army under the leadership of Amr ibn al-As (RA) conquered Egypt.

items.title: Ghazwaye Abwa (Waddan)
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) himself led the first military campaign. A peace treaty was made with the Banu Jamra tribe.

items.title: Death of Abdul Muttalib, grandfather of the Prophet (peace be upon him).
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) lost his grandfather Abdul Muttalib at the age of eight. He then grew up under the supervision of uncle Abu Talib.

items.title: The incident of Bir Mauna
items.description: 70 Hafez were martyred by deceiving the Companions of the Qur'an. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was revealed in Qunut for 30 days.

items.title: Razi's incident
items.description: 6 Companions were deceived and sold to the polytheists. Khubayb (ra) prayed two rakats before he was martyred.

items.title: Ghazwaye Banu Nadir
items.description: The Jewish tribe of Banu Nadi plotted to kill the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and were expelled from Madinah. Surah Hashar was revealed.

items.title: Sariya Nakhla
items.description: The expedition led by Abdullah Ibn Jahsh (R.A.). First armed conflict with Quraysh.

items.title: Marriage of Ali (RA) and Fatima (RA).
items.description: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) married his beloved daughter Fatimah to Ali (RA).

items.title: Battle of Siffin
items.description: Battle of Siffin between Ali (RA) and Muawiya (RA). Later terminated by arbitration.

items.title: Death of Imam Hasan (RA).
items.description: Hasan (R.A.), the son-in-law of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the leader of the heavenly youth, passed away in Madinah.

items.title: First migration to Habsha
items.description: When persecution increased in Makkah, 11 male and 4 female Companions migrated to Abyssinia (Ethiopia), the land of righteous Najashi.

items.title: Invitation to Darul Arkam
items.description: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to conduct Da'wah secretly in the house of Arqam Ibn Abil Arqam (R.A.) at the foot of Safa Hill.

items.title: Rise of Musaylamatul Qayyab
items.description: After the death of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), the hypocrite Prophet Musaylama falsely claimed prophethood in Yamama.

items.title: Birth of Imam Malek (RA).
items.description: Imam Malik Ibn Anas (RA) was born in Madinah, author of Muatta Imam Malik and founder of the Maliki Madhhab.

items.title: Battle of Wakedi
items.description: In Iraq, Khalid bin Walid (RA) defeated the Persian forces and paved the way for the conquest of Iraq.

items.title: Death of Ibn Taymiyyah (RA).
items.description: Shaykhul Islam Imam Ibn Taymiyyah (RA) died in prison in Damascus.

items.title: Beginning of the illness of the Prophet (peace be upon him).
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) fell ill which continued till his death in Rabiul Awal.

items.title: Death of Ibn Mas'ud (RA).
items.description: Renowned Sahabi, Hafiz of Quran and Mufassir Abdullah Ibn Masood (RA) passed away in Madinah.

items.title: Birth of the Prophet (peace be upon him).
items.description: Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was born in Makkah on Monday morning of Amul Fiel (571 AD). His father Abdullah died before he was born.

items.title: Nurture by Halima Sadia
items.description: According to traditional Arab custom, the baby Muhammad (may peace be upon him) was given to Halima Sadiya of the Banu Saad tribe to nurse.

items.title: The death of the mother of the Prophet (peace be upon him).
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) lost his mother Amena bint Wahhab at the age of six. Then he was brought up by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib.

items.title: Ghazwaye Saweek
items.description: When Abu Sufyan attacked the outskirts of Madinah, he left the umbrella (Sawiq) while fleeing.

items.title: Death of Abu Talib
items.description: Abu Talib, the uncle and guardian of the Prophet (peace be upon him) passed away.

items.title: Hijrat and Quba Mosque in Medina
items.title_ar: الْهِجْرَةُ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَبِنَاءُ مَسْجِدِ قُبَاء
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) reached Quba and built the first mosque of Islam, 'Masjid Quba'.

items.title: First Friday prayer
items.description: On the way of Hijrah, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) offered the first Friday prayer in the history of Islam in the valley of the tribe of Banu Salim.

items.title: Death of the Prophet (peace be upon him).
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) died on Monday at the age of 63. His last words were 'Ar-Rafiqul A'la'.

items.title: Abu Bakr's (RA) acceptance of the caliphate
items.description: Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was elected as the first Caliph by consensus of Banu Sa'ida.

items.title: Construction of Masjid Nabawi
items.description: On reaching Medina, the construction of Masjid an-Nabawi began at the place where the camel of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) sat.

items.title: Formulation of Madinah Sanad
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) drew up a written charter of peaceful coexistence between the Muhajirs, the Ansar and the Jews. It is considered to be the first written constitution in the world.

items.title: Muakhat — Establishment of brotherhood
items.description: He established a bond of brotherhood between the Muhajirs and the Ansar.

items.title: Prevalence of call to prayer
items.description: Abdullah Ibn Zayd (RA) saw the call to prayer in a dream and the Prophet (PBUH) appointed Bilal (RA) as the first muezzin.

items.title: Death of Abdur Rahman Ibn Awf (RA).
items.description: Asharae Mubasshara and Badri Sahabi Abdur Rahman Ibn Awf (RA) passed away in Madinah.

items.title: Dispatch of Usama forces
items.description: Abu Bakr (R.A.) sent the army of Usama Ibn Zayd (R.A.) against the Romans as per the instructions of the Prophet (Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam).

items.title: Birth of Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal (RA).
items.description: Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal (RA) was born in Baghdad, one of the Imams of the Four Madhhabs and the compiler of Musnad Ahmad.

items.title: Invitation to Tawaif
items.description: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) who was persecuted in Makkah went to Tawaif and gave an invitation. The people there stoned him to death.

items.title: Najashi Raja's conversion to Islam
items.description: Najashi, the righteous king of Habsha (Ethiopia) secretly converted to Islam. Upon his death, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) performed the Ghaibana funeral.

items.title: Gazwaye Buwat
items.description: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) followed the commercial caravan of Quraysh with 200 companions.

items.title: Ghazwaye Safwan (Badre Ula)
items.description: When Qurz ibn Jabir looted the camels of Madinah, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) followed him.

items.title: The Battle of Ridda begins
items.description: When the hypocrite Prophet Musaylama, Tulaiha and Sajah rebelled, Abu Bakr (R.A.) sent 11 troops.

items.title: Gazwaye Gaba (Zi-Karad)
items.description: Salama Ibnul Aqwa (R.A.) alone chased the enemy and recovered the looted camels.

items.title: Abdul Quader Jilani (Rah.) passed away
items.description: The famous scholar and Ali Sheikh Abdul Quader Jilani of Baghdad passed away.

items.title: The decision to compile the Qur'an
items.description: Abu Bakr (RA) decided to compile the Quran on the advice of Omar (RA) after 700 Hafez were martyred in Yamama. Zayd Ibn Thabit (RA) was given the responsibility.

items.title: Muhammad Ibnul Qasim Conquest of Indus
items.description: Muhammad Ibnul Qasim, who was only 17 years old, conquered the province of Sindh in the subcontinent.

items.title: Death of Bilal (RA).
items.description: The first muezzin of Islam and a freed slave, Bilal Ibn Rabah (RA) passed away in Damascus.

items.title: Birth of Imam Nawabi (RA).
items.description: Imam Nawabi (RA), the author of Riyadus Salehin and Arbain Nawabi, was born in Nawa, Syria.

items.title: Death of Saad Ibn Abi Waqqas (RA).
items.description: The last member of the Asharai Mubashshara, the conqueror of Qadesia and the founder of Kufa, Sa'd (RA) passed away in Madinah.

items.title: Spread of Islam in Iraq
items.description: Khalid Bin Waleed (RA) conquered the city of Hira and opened the doors of Islam to Iraq.

items.title: Martyrdom of Zubair Ibnul Awam (RA).
items.description: Zubair (may Allah be pleased with him) one of the Mubassharas of Ashara and a follower of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was martyred on his way back after the Battle of Jamal.

items.title: Battle of Mutah
items.description: 3,000 Muslim soldiers faced 1,000,000 Romans. Zayd, Jafar and Abdullah (RA) were martyred successively.

items.title: Martyrdom of Jafar Ibn Abi Talib (RA).
items.description: In the Battle of Mutah, Jafar (R.A.) got his two hands cut off while fighting with the flag. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that Allah gave him two wings.

items.title: Khalid bin Waleed (R.A.) was given the title of 'Saifullah'
items.description: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) gave Khalid the title of 'Saifullah' (Sword of God) after bringing the Muslim army back safely from Mutah.

items.title: Birth of Zainab bint Ali (RA).
items.description: Zainab (RA) was born to Ali (RA) and Fatima (RA).

items.title: Ghazwaye Dhul Ashira
items.description: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) followed the caravan of Quraysh heading towards Syria. This caravan later led to the Battle of Badr.

items.title: Battle of Yarmouk
items.description: 40 thousand Muslims under the leadership of Khalid bin Walid (RA) defeated 200,000 Roman soldiers and conquered Syria.

items.title: Death of Abu Ubaidah Ibnul Jarrah (RA).
items.description: One of the Companions of Asharai Mubashshara, entitled 'Aminul Ummah' (Trustee of the Ummah) died of plague.

items.title: Death of Mu'az Ibn Jabal (RA).
items.description: The most knowledgeable Companion on Halal and Haram, Mu'adh (R.A.) died of the Plague of Amwas in the region of Sham.

items.title: First attempt at the siege of Constantinople
items.description: During the reign of Muawiyah (R.A.), the Muslim navy besieged Constantinople (Istanbul) for the first time. Abu Ayyub Ansari (RA) was martyred in this campaign.

items.title: Martyrdom of Abu Ayyub Ansari (RA).
items.description: The great companion in whose house the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) first stayed after his migration to Madinah died during the siege of Constantinople.

items.title: Battle of Nahawand
items.description: In this battle known as 'Fathul Futuh' (Victory of all victories), the Muslims decisively defeated the Persians.

items.title: Death of Imam Abu Yusuf (RA).
items.description: Imam Abu Yusuf (r.a.), chief student of Imam Abu Hanifa and chief justice of the Abbasid Caliphate, passed away.

items.title: Death of Fatimah (RA).
items.description: Six months after the death of the Prophet (peace be upon him), his beloved daughter, the leader of the heavenly women, Fatimah (RA) passed away.

items.title: Battle of Yamama
items.description: Valor of Wahshi (RA) and Abu Dujana (RA) against the Hypocritical Prophet Musaylama. 700 Hafez was martyred.

items.title: Khalid's (ra) Iraq campaign began
items.description: Khalid Bin Walid (R.A.) started the Iraq campaign under the command of Abu Bakr (R.A.) and won one victory after another.

items.title: Death of Imam Ghazali (RA).
items.description: The great Islamic thinker and philosopher known as 'Hujjatul Islam' Imam Ghazali (RA) passed away.

items.title: Plague of Amwas
items.description: 25 thousand Muslims died in the terrible plague in Palestine, including great Companions like Abu Ubaidah and Mu'az (RA).

items.title: Death of Abu Bakr (RA).
items.description: The first Caliph Abu Bakr (RA) died at the age of 63. He was buried next to the Prophet (peace be upon him).

items.title: Accepting the caliphate of Umar (RA).
items.description: According to the will of Abu Bakr (RA), Umar (RA) was appointed as the second caliph.

items.title: Establishment of Baitul Mal
items.description: Umar (RA) established the state treasury 'Baytul Maal', from which the allowances of the people and government expenditure were carried out.

items.title: Martyrdom of Talha Ibn Ubaidullah (RA).
items.description: Talha (ra) one of Mubashshara's Companions was martyred in the Battle of Jamal.

items.title: Birth of Ibnul Asir (RA).
items.description: Ibn al-Asir (RA), the author of al-Kamil Fit Tarikh and Islamic historian, was born in Mosul.

items.title: Isra and Miraj
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) went from Makkah to Baitul Muqaddas (Isra) and from there to Sidratul Muntaha (Miraj). Five times prayer is obligatory.

items.title: Gazwaye Tabuk
items.description: The Last Ghazwa of the Prophet (peace be upon him). Journey to Tabu with 30 thousand companions. Uthman (RA) donated 1000 camels.

items.title: Birth of Ali (RA).
items.description: Ali, the fourth caliph and cousin of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was born inside the Kaaba.

items.title: Conquest of Baitul Muqaddas by Saladin
items.description: After 90 years, Sultan Salahuddin recaptured Baitul Muqaddas from the Ayyubid Crusaders.

items.title: Acceptance of Baitul Muqaddas by Umar (RA).
items.description: Umar (RA) himself went and received the keys of Jerusalem peacefully. Christians are given all religious freedom.

items.title: Birth of Imam Shafi'i (RA).
items.description: One of the four schools of thought, Imam Shafi'i (RA) was born in Gaza.

items.title: Death of Omar Ibn Abdul Aziz (RA).
items.description: The fifth caliph Rashid and the righteous caliph Omar bin Abdul Aziz (r.a.) passed away.

items.title: Conquest of Constantinople
items.description: Sultan Muhammad II (Muhammad al-Fatih) conquered Constantinople as prophesied by the Prophet (peace be upon him).

items.title: Death of Anas Ibn Malik (RA).
items.description: Anas (R.A.), the 10-year servant of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the narrator of many hadiths, died in Basra as the last companion.

items.title: Birth of Ibn Khaldun (RA).
items.description: Ibn Khaldun, father of sociology and author of 'Al-Muqaddimah', was born in Tunis.

items.title: Battle of Taifuluj
items.description: After the conquest of Makkah and Hunayn, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) besieged Tawaif.

items.title: Death of Imam Muslim (RA).
items.description: Compiler of Sahih Muslim, Imam Muslim Ibnul Hajjaz (RA) passed away in Nishapur.

items.title: Shabbat
items.description: Rajini in the middle of the month of Shaban. On this night, Allah forgives many people.

items.title: Qibla change
items.description: Qibla changes from Baitul Muqaddas towards Kaaba. Verse 144 of Surah Baqarah was revealed.

items.title: Fasting is obligatory
items.description: In the 2nd Hijri, the 183rd verse of Surah Baqarah was revealed, making the fasting of Ramadan obligatory.

items.title: Ghazway Banu Mustaliq
items.description: On the way back from this battle, Aisha (RA) was slandered by Ifq. His sanctity is declared in Surah Noor Najil.

items.title: Birth of Hussain (RA).
items.description: Hussain (RA) was born, the son-in-law of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and the leader of the heavenly youth.

items.title: Zakat is obligatory
items.description: Zakat was imposed on Muslims in 2nd Hijri.

items.title: Death of Abbas (RA).
items.description: The uncle of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) Abbas (RA) died in Madinah. The Abbasid Caliphate is named after him.

items.title: Birth of Hasan (RA).
items.description: The first son of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) Hassan (RA) was born. The Prophet (peace be upon him) himself named him.

items.title: Verses were revealed with the permission of Jihad
items.description: Muslims are permitted to fight in self-defense through verses 39-40 of Surah Hajj.

items.title: Death of Ibnul Qayyim (RA).
items.description: Ibn al-Qayyim (r.a.), the author of Jadul Maad and a favorite student of Ibn Taymiyyah, passed away in Damascus.

items.title: Preparations for the battle of Badr began
items.description: Hearing the caravan of Quraysh coming, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) began to gather the Companions.

items.title: Death of Imam Tirmidhi (RA).
items.description: Imam Tirmidhi (RA), the compiler of Sunan Tirmidhi and Shamaile Muhammadi, passed away.

items.title: The beginning of the revelation of the Qur'an
items.description: In the cave of Hera, Gabriel (A.S.) brought the first five verses of Surah Al-Alak. The Qur'an began to be revealed.

items.title: The sahifahs are revealed
items.description: Narrated that the sahifah of Ibrahim (as) was revealed at the beginning of this month.

items.title: Birth of Abdullah Ibn Omar (RA).
items.description: Abdullah ibn Umar (R.A.), one of the Companions who gave the most fatwas, was born.

items.title: Acceptance of Islam by Sa'd Ibn Mu'az (RA).
items.description: Sa'd Ibn Mu'az (R.A.), the chief of the tribe of Aws, accepted Islam and his whole tribe became Muslims.

items.title: Death of Khadijah (RA).
items.description: The first wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the first convert to Islam. This year is 'Amul Hujan' (year of mourning).

items.title: The Torah was revealed
items.description: It is narrated that on this day the Torah was revealed to Musa (a.s.).

items.title: The Bible was revealed
items.description: It is narrated that on this day the Injil was revealed to Jesus (pbuh).

items.title: Historical Battle of Badr
items.description: 313 Companions won a historic victory against 1000 Quraysh. 70 Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl were killed.

items.title: Death of Ayesha (RA).
items.description: Ayesha Siddiqa, beloved wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and narrator of many hadiths, passed away at the age of 66.

items.title: Conquest of Mecca
items.description: Victory of Mecca without bloodshed with an army of 10,000 Companions. Removal of 360 idols of Kaaba and declaration of amnesty.

items.title: Martyrdom of Ali (RA).
items.description: The fourth caliph Ali (RA) was martyred in Kufa after being hit by Khareji Ibn Muljim.

items.title: Birth of Imam Bukhari (RA).
items.description: Imam Bukhari (RA) the compiler of the greatest hadith book Sahih Bukhari was born in Bukhara.

items.title: Shabba Kadar
items.description: A resin is better than a thousand months. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to seek it on the odd night of the last decade.

items.title: Conquest of Andalusia (Spain).
items.description: Tariq bin Ziyad defeated King Roderick in Spain and started 800 years of Islamic civilization.

items.title: Ain Zalut's War
items.description: Sultan Qutuz and Baibars saved the Muslim world by defeating the formidable Mongol forces.

items.title: Battle of Hittin
items.description: Salah al-Din defeated the main force of the Ayyubid Crusaders at Hittin, which paved the way for the conquest of Baitul Muqaddas.

items.title: Eid-ul-Fitr
items.description: Eid-ul-Fitr is the biggest religious festival of Muslims after Ramadan.

items.title: Death of Imam Bukhari (RA).
items.description: Imam Bukhari (RA), the author of Sahih Bukhari, passed away in Samarkand on the night of Eid.

items.title: Treaty of Hasan (RA) and Muawiya (RA).
items.description: Hasan (RA) handed over the caliphate to Muawiya (RA) for the unity of the Muslim Ummah. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) predicted that this grandson would make a treaty between the two parties.

items.title: Ghazwaye Ohud
items.description: Battle with the Quraish at Mount Ohud. 70 people including Hamza (ra) were martyred. A temporary disaster ensued as the archers left their positions.

items.title: Martyrdom of Hamza (RA).
items.description: Hamza (RA), the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) and the lion of Islam, was martyred by the spear of Wahshi in Ohud.

items.title: Accidental death
items.description: War against the Hawazin tribe after the conquest of Makkah. It is mentioned in the Quran (Sura Tawbah 25).

items.title: Ghazwaye Khandak (Ahzab)
items.description: 10 thousand polytheists attacked Medina. The trenches were dug on the advice of Salman Farsi (RA).

items.title: Ghazway Banu Qurayza
items.description: Campaign against the treacherous Banu Qurayza tribe. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (R.A.) ruled on the law of the Torah.

items.title: The siege of Taif is over
items.description: The Prophet (peace be upon him) lifted the siege of Taif and prayed for them. Later the whole of Taif became Muslim.

items.title: Jamal's War
items.description: A tragic clash took place in Basra between the forces of Ali (RA) and the forces of Ayesha, Talha and Zubair (RA).

items.title: Birth of Ibn Hajar Askalani (RA).
items.description: Hafez Ibn Hajar Asqalani (RA) the author of Fathul Bari (Bukhari's greatest exegesis) was born in Egypt.

items.title: Treaty of Hudaybiyah
items.description: Umrah journey with 1400 companions. The treaty with the Quraysh is called 'Fathum Mubeen' in the Qur'an.

items.title: Bayatur Ridwan
items.description: The companions swore to fight to the death under the tree. Allah is pleased with them.

items.title: Umratul Qaza
items.description: According to the terms of the treaty, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) performed Umrah in Makkah with 2000 companions.

items.title: Construction of Kaaba House (Ibrahim A.)
items.description: Ibrahim (A.S.) and Ismail (A.S.) rebuilt the Kaaba House together.

items.title: Birth of Imam Abu Hanifa (RA).
items.description: Imam Azam Abu Hanifa Numan bin Thabit (R.H.) was born in Kufa, the founder of Hanafi fiqh.

items.title: Victory of Damascus
items.description: Damascus, the capital of Syria, was conquered under the joint leadership of Khalid bin Walid and Abu Ubaidah (RA).

items.title: Death of Abdullah Ibn Abbas (RA).
items.description: The great Sahabah Ibn Abbas (R.A.) with the title of 'Tarjumanul Qur'an' (Explainer of the Qur'an) passed away in Taif.

items.title: Death of Ibn Hisham (RA).
items.description: Ibn Hisham, compiler of Sirat Ibn Hisham and biographer of the Prophet (peace be upon him) died in Egypt.

items.title: Death of Umm Salama (RA).
items.description: Umm al-Mu'minin and two Companions of Hijrat Umm Salama (RA) passed away in Madinah.

items.title: The status of the month of Zilkad
items.description: Zilqad is one of the four haram (honorable) months. Fighting is forbidden in this month. Hajj preparations are made.

items.title: Day of Arafah and prayer
items.description: The greatest day of the year. On this day, Allah releases the most people from hell. Two years of sins are forgiven if you fast.

items.title: Farewell Hajj and Arafa speech
items.description: The only Hajj of a lifetime with 1 lakh companions. Banning human rights, women's rights and usury.

items.title: Declaring the perfection of religion
items.description: It was revealed on the plain of Arafah: 'Today I have fulfilled your religion' (Surah Ma'idah 3).

items.title: Eid al-Adha and Qurbani
items.description: Eid-ul-Azha commemorates the great sacrifice of Ibrahim (AS). Qurbani, Takbeer, Tashreek and Eid prayers.

items.title: Sacrifice of Ibrahim (AS).
items.description: When Ibrahim (a.s.) went to sacrifice his son Ismail by Allah's command, Allah sent Dumba.

items.title: Ayame Tashreek
items.description: The days of stoning and remembrance in Mina. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said that these are days of eating and drinking and remembrance of Allah.

items.title: Martyrdom of Uthman (RA).
items.description: After 40 days of siege, the third Caliph Uthman (RA) was martyred while reciting the Quran.

items.title: Compilation of the Qur'an (Mushaf Usmani)
items.description: Uthman (RA) made a standard copy of the Quran and sent it to different cities. It is known as 'Mushafe Usmani'.

items.title: Accepting the caliphate of Ali (RA).
items.description: Ali (RA) became the fourth and last Caliph after the martyrdom of Uthman (RA).

items.title: Gadire Khum's speech
items.description: On the way back from Farewell Hajj, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) addressed the Companions at a place called Ghadir Khum.

items.title: Attack on Omar (RA).
items.description: Abu Lulu Firoz stabbed during Fajr prayer. Umar (RA) formed the Shura Committee and was martyred on 1 Muharram.

items.title: Death of Abu Zar Giffari (RA).
items.description: Abu Zar (R.A.), the great companion of Juhad and Tawakkul, died alone in Rabajah.
